name: Henry Samueli
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2000-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Henry Samueli is cofounder of chipmaker Broadcom. He stepped down as chairman in June 2026 but is still a director.
Samueli started Broadcom with fellow billionaire Henry Nicholas in 1991 in a Redondo Beach, California condominium.
Samueli and his wife bought the NHL's Anaheim Ducks for $70 million in 2005. The franchise is now worth more than $1 billion.
The Samuelis donated $200 million to the University of California, Irvine in 2017. The gift was the largest in the school's history.
forbes_facts: Samueli is the son of Polish Holocaust survivors.
Samueli holds over 75 patents and is a recipient of the Marconi Society Prize for his innovations.

name: Eric Lefkofsky
sec_insider_companies: Tempus AI, Inc. (TEM) - CEO and Chairman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Eric Lefkofsky made his fortune from the daily deals site Groupon, which he founded in 2008 with  Andrew Mason and longtime business partner Brad Keywell.
Lefkofsky founded and now runs healthcare startup Tempus, which uses data to improve cancer treatment.
Tempus went public at a $6 billion valuation in 2024, his fourth IPO.
Together Lefkofsky and Keywell also founded VC firm Lightbank, which has made investments in over 100 companies, including social media firm Sprout Social.
Lefkofsky grew up outside of Detroit and went to the University of Michigan for his undergraduate and law degrees.
forbes_facts: Lefkofsky and Keywell owned stakes in the Wrigley Building located on Chicago's Magnificent Mile but sold them in 2018.
After a girlfriend dumped him in college, Lefkofsky started his first business, selling carpets. He estimates he generated hundreds of thousands of dollars in sales.

name: Lisa Su
sec_insider_companies: ADVANCED MICRO DEVICES INC (AMD) - Chair, President & CEO
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Lisa Su, the CEO of semiconductor firm Advanced Micro Devices, has led one of the greatest recent turnarounds in the technology sector.
In 2025 the company announced a partnership with OpenAI (the creator of ChatGPT), highlighting the use of AMD chips for computing power.
Next, she's preparing for battle against Nvidia in the AI revolution, and expects to keep winning; Nvidia is run by her distant relative Jensen Huang.
The daughter of a mathematician and a bookkeeper turned entrepreneur, Su was born in Tainan, Taiwan, in 1969, and immigrated to New York City at age 3.
After graduating from the Bronx High School of Science, Su went to MIT, where she earned a bachelor's (and later a Ph.D.) in electrical engineering because it seemed to be the most difficult major.
She did stints at Texas Instruments, IBM and Freescale, then joined AMD in 2012 and became CEO two years later.
forbes_facts: During her time at IBM, Su worked directly with highly respected CEO Lou Gerstner.

name: Feridun Gecgel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Feridun Gecgel chairs Astor Enerji, Turkey's largest manufacturer of transformers and switching products.
He owns nearly 80% of the company, which went public in Istanbul in 2023.
Gecgel started his first business in furniture production. In 2005, he entered the transformer industry by purchasing Astor, which he bought for $3 million 20 years ago.

He was born in Şanlıurfa in 1970 and after graduating high school, became an entrepreneur, starting at Özgüney Elektrik, where he established his own company, specializing in the sale of electrical and electronic materials.

name: Edward Screven
forbes_bio: Edward Screven is the former chief corporate architect of Oracle.
He worked at the company for over 38 years before retiring in February 2025.
Screven was responsible for many of Oracle's best-known open-source programs including Java, Oracle Linux, MySQL, and VirtualBox.
He also served as Oracle's representative on the board of chip designer Ampere Computing and planned to continue in that role after retiring from Oracle.
SoftBank agreed to acquire Ampere for $6.5 billion in March 2025. Oracle owned nearly a third of Ampere at the time.
